questions.question: To choose the right placard for hazardous materials, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers being used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: Placards show the hazard class of materials being transported. They are placed on the outside of vehicles to warn others.

questions.question: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for:
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep shipping papers for at least two years after materials are picked up. For hazardous waste, the time is three years.

questions.question: To get a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, which agency does the background check?
questions.explanation: You must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: While driving, where should shipping papers be kept?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. Place them in the driver's door pouch or another location where they are easy to find and clearly visible.

questions.question: To get a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, which agency does the background check?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) performs a federal security check for new or renewed HazMat endorsements.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a railroad crossing while carrying chlorine?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must reduce your speed before crossing the tracks.
You may proceed across the tracks without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine, you must always stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track before crossing the railroad. This applies even if no train is visible.

questions.question: What symbol shows that something is a marine pollutant?

options.text: Waves in a yellow triangle with an X through them
A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it
A bird in a red octagon

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant marking is a fish in a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, what should you not use?
questions.explanation: Never use hooks or equipment that could damage containers. Always handle hazardous materials carefully to protect the containers and packaging.

questions.question: If your engine powers a pump for delivery, when should you turn off the engine?
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine before unhooking the hoses when you are done transferring product. If your engine does not power the pump, turn it off during loading and unloading.

questions.question: How far away from a placard for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials must a person be to smoke?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (flammable gases) materials. Never smoke near any flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating required on vehicles carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Explosive materials are classified as what type of hazard?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include explosives and items that can catch fire or explode.

questions.question: How do drivers know when a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: By placards posted on the truck
By flashing lights on the truck
By the driver waving an arm out the window

questions.correctAnswerText: By placards posted on the truck
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped placards are placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If hazardous materials catch fire while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
Continue driving to the fire department

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and equipment. Call emergency personnel and let them handle it.

questions.question: How must placards be positioned on a vehicle?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible
So words and numbers read from left to right
Within three inches of other markings

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right
questions.explanation: Placards must be positioned so words and numbers read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: Which requirement does NOT apply to a person loading a hazardous materials tank?

options.text: Must be within 10 feet of the tank
Must know the hazards of the materials
Must be authorized to move the tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be within 10 feet of the tank
questions.explanation: The person in charge must be alert, aware of hazards, authorized to move the tank, and within 25 feet (not 10 feet) of the tank.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information to drivers?
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must give drivers emergency response information.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials employees must receive training and testing at least once every three years.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide
In the Periodic Table of Elements

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide contains information about hazardous chemicals, indexed by shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: If you discover hazardous materials leaking from your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call the National Response Center
Leave the area to find help

questions.explanation: If hazardous materials are leaking, park the vehicle as soon as possible to stop the spread of contamination and reduce cleanup costs.

questions.question: When accepting a shipment, what sign shows the cargo may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Take proper safety steps when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: Shippers must warn drivers and others about hazardous material risks. They do this by putting warning labels on packages, adding placards to vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency information.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the trip is fewer than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards cannot be driven except in emergencies to protect people or property.

questions.question: If a package has liquid containers, what must be on the package?

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must show arrows pointing the correct upright direction. Place these packages facing the correct way.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo is leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone and call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous cargo leaks, do not drive more than needed. Driving spreads contamination. Stop the vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If no phone is available, send someone else for help.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper include?

options.text: The location of fire departments on the route.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must include an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: What license is needed to drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a commercial driver license with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials, even if not carrying them at that moment.

questions.question: Is a shipping paper required for hazardous materials?

options.text: Can be kept as a digital file only.

questions.explanation: Shippers must provide shipping papers for all hazardous materials to communicate the material risks.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?
questions.explanation: The material's ID number must appear on the shipping paper and packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and bulk packaging.

questions.question: What must be in a vehicle carrying chlorine?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved.

questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must keep an approved gas mask and emergency kit in their vehicle.
